addc.title: Add Connector
addc.titleLocal: Add Connector Started as a Command
addc.sub: A connector is an MCP server that gives Her more tools. Paste its address or the command that starts it; Her checks the rest.
addc.name: Name
addc.nameNote: Shown in the list, and the prefix of its tools' names.
addc.nameNoteSuggested: Shown in the list, and the prefix of its tools' names. Press Tab to fill in {{name}}, or leave it empty to use it.
addc.badName: Letters, digits, - and _ only, at most 32 characters
addc.taken: There is a connector named {{name}} already; choose another name

bad.empty: Enter an address or a command
bad.json: This looks like JSON, but it does not parse
bad.jsonServer: No server in the JSON (it needs command or url)
bad.scheme: A remote address starts with http:// or https://

addc.willCheck: Her checks first whether it needs a sign-in
addc.insecure: not https: a token would travel in clear text

note.apiKey: No sign-in settings published; it probably takes an API key

addc.oauthDesc: Sign in with your {{issuer}} account in the browser; the token is kept on this environment's machine and renewed when it expires.
addc.ownDesc: An app you registered with the provider, for example when your company requires a fixed client ID.
addc.secretOptional: Optional, kept in the credential store
addc.redirect: When registering the app with {{issuer}}, set the callback address to
addc.tokenDesc: Puts the token the provider gave you in a request header. For servers that take an API key instead of OAuth.
addc.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token; it goes to the credential store
addc.tokenRefused: The server refused this token (HTTP 401). Check that it is right and allowed.
addc.noneDesc: The server is open; Her connects directly.
addc.httpDesc: The current MCP transport. Use it unless the server only supports SSE.
addc.sseDesc: The older transport being phased out. Chosen when the address ends in /sse.
addc.trust: Only add connectors from developers you trust. Which tools a connector offers and what they return is up to its developer; Her cannot verify it or promise it will not change.
addc.download: The first run of {{program}} downloads first; the check may take a while.
addc.localTrust: A command runs as you on this environment's machine and can read and write what you can there. Only add commands you trust. Your device asks you to approve it, with Touch ID on a Mac.
addc.envNote: Variables whose names look like secrets are locked: their values go to the credential store and the configuration holds only a reference. Click the lock to switch.
addc.loginTitle: Sign in to {{name}} in your browser
addc.loginText: The sign-in page of {{issuer}} is open in your browser. After you sign in and allow access, come back here.
addc.approveText: Your device shows the command {{name}} runs and asks you to approve it, with Touch ID on a Mac.

found.open: Checked: the server accepted the connection; no authentication needed.
found.oauth: Checked: the server asks you to sign in; its sign-in service is {{issuer}}.
found.oauthOwn: Checked: the server asks you to sign in, but {{issuer}} does not let apps register on their own, so it needs your own OAuth app.
found.token: Checked: the server needs authentication but publishes no sign-in service; it most likely wants a token or API key.
found.unreached: Checked: the address didn't answer this time; below are the saved settings.

what.token: The token is kept in the credential store; the configuration holds only a reference.

addc.patHint: If the provider also offers personal access tokens, choosing "Token or API key" is simpler.
addc.clientAutoDesc: Her registers itself with the sign-in service; nothing to set up.
addc.clientAutoOff: {{issuer}} does not let apps register on their own
addc.duplicate: {{name}} already reaches this service; one connector per service is enough.
addc.saved: Saved in the credential store · type a new value to replace it
